html:
Peter Chanel was a French priest of the Marist order who was killed on the island of Futuna in 1841. He became the first Catholic martyr and saint of Oceania.

He reached Futuna in 1837 and lived there for nearly four years, winning a few converts. When the king's own son asked for baptism, men loyal to the king killed Chanel with a club.

Within a short time most of Futuna had become Catholic, as had nearby Wallis under the Marists. He was made a saint in 1954. The islands remain almost wholly Catholic, and the church is a pillar of island life under French rule. See also Pierre Bataillon, the Marist on Wallis.
